finding_1.impact: A panel callback can outlive device removal. If the module is later unloaded, the notifier may retain callback and client-data addresses in released module text/data. The module-exit path also calls netlink_exit before platform_driver_unregister, so notifier callbacks can overlap netlink teardown. No runtime failure was reproduced.

sequence: the first character-device open requests the IRQ
the last file release disables and frees the IRQ
gf_remove removes fp_wakelock and other device resources but does not disable or free the IRQ
finding_2.impact: If the platform device is unbound while a file is open, the IRQ may remain live until that file closes and can run after the wakeup source has been removed. This is an unverified lifetime/teardown gap, not a demonstrated invalid memory access.

module_exit_order: Ghidra stock cleanup_module and source zte_fp_exit call netlink_exit first
platform_driver_unregister runs afterwards and invokes gf_remove
the notifier worker and any live IRQ have not been drained before netlink teardown begins
